risks.note: The Company reports large individual order fulfilments to single clients (e.g. 45 reactors and 21 process equipment units delivered to a single client in Maharashtra), and changes in customer capital expenditure plans are flagged as a threat, indicating exposure to a concentrated customer base.

The Company faces significant competition from other companies in the Indian markets it operates in; some competitors have greater resources and/or a more widely recognised brand, which may give them a competitive advantage over BEW.
Volatility in raw material prices is flagged as a threat that could affect production costs and profitability.
The Company is exposed to fluctuation in the rupee and foreign exchange volatility, which affects earnings from exports and outgo on imports.
The Company finances operations through a combination of internal accruals and bank borrowings; an increase in prevailing interest rates may lead to higher finance costs and impact profitability.
The Company is exposed to credit risk on receivables from clients and manages this through credit limit approval procedures and financial health research on clients before entering agreements.

The Company is subject to changes in Indian law, regulation, government policy and accounting principles as a company regulated under the Companies Act and supervised by statutory/regulatory authorities.
The Company flags supply-chain disruptions as a threat alongside rising competition and raw material price fluctuations.
